journey.name: Signup — a paid-for token survives the app dying
journey.description:
The invariant that costs real money if it breaks. A signup token is single-use and never expires, and by the time Loopky holds one the user has already spent an SMS attempt (two per week) or paid sats. If the app is killed between obtaining the token and registering the account, the next launch must spend that same token — otherwise they pay twice.
Loopky redeems the token itself now (9372ff86), so the window is the "signup_local_progress" step: the token is stored as `PendingSignup.Redeemable` when verification succeeds, and the key is stored before `signUp` runs.
**Expected to fail as of 2026-10-16, from reading the code — not yet driven.** "Create a Pubky" always opens the method screen, which never consults the stored token (#510); the local step is reached only by finishing a method again, and starting Lightning again calls `createInvoice`, which overwrites the stored token with a new pending invoice. Record the result in the PR that runs this.
Use the invite-code method to probe it for free (the code IS the token, so re-entering it is the honest fallback, but a user who paid by SMS or Lightning has no code to re-enter). Requires the same setup as `17-signup-invite-code.xml` and a freshly minted staging token.

actions.action: From a signed-out Loopky, tap "onboarding_create_pubky", then "signup_method_invite"
Turn airplane mode ON, so registration stalls on "signup_local_progress" with the token already stored
Tap "signup_invite_input", type a freshly minted XXXX-XXXX-XXXX token, tap "signup_invite_submit"
While "signup_local_progress" (or its error) is on screen, kill the app outright: adb shell am force-stop com.github.jvsena42.loopky. Note the pubky in logcat ("registerKey: registering …")
Turn airplane mode OFF and relaunch: adb shell am start -n com.github.jvsena42.loopky/.MainActivity
Verify logcat shows "init: no persisted session" — signing up never completed, so there is no session

THE INVARIANT. Tap "onboarding_create_pubky" and verify Loopky offers to finish the signup with the stored token — WITHOUT asking for a verification method again — and registers the SAME pubky noted above
Verify logcat shows no second Homegate request for a token, and no "registerKey" for a different pubky — a fresh key would strand the first identity, and a fresh token would charge the user twice
If instead the method screen appears: that is the failure described above. Do NOT pay to probe the Lightning branch; record the finding instead
